title: Larry starting the night shift in the radio van
description: Larry, pen in one hand and eraser in the other, looks up from his work inside the radio van at the start of a twelve-hour night shift he worked alone. Behind him a whiteboard lists Vietnamese place names with UTM grid coordinates; the quarter-hour scheduling racks stand at right. His name tape — HUNNEW… — shows over his pocket.
larrysRecollection:
This is me inside the radio van starting the night 12-hour shift alone

Rosethorn 007 was a aircraft call sign I would use. It was the helicopter that we had access to.
When I wanted to get out of here, I would call Captain Guetler.
researchNotes: Larry's own confirmation (Memories comments, 2026-08-15; archived as data/recollections/giscus-vn-0015-c18032414.json and -c18032583.json) of what the survey read from the HUNNEW... name tape. Working detail established: twelve-hour night shifts, alone. The second comment ties the Rosethorn 007 call sign — his lifeline off remote sites — to Captain Guegler, here spelled 'Guetler' (a new phonetic variant for the person record). The place/grid board behind him still merits full magnified transcription; its Saigon-area center of gravity supports the Tân Sơn Nhứt headquarters hypothesis.
